liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Box Of Rain** (3 reviews): Reviewer, who attended, singles out Box of Rain and the whole second set; Crowd erupted when Box of Rain began, and again when Phil's singing revealed what it was [29][31][32]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (2 reviews): Saint is described as super rockin' in a strong second set; Reviewer says this was the last Lost Sailor/Saint pairing with Garcia [26][30]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 other source): A Promised Land tease comes before Greatest Story [4]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Emotional Half-Step opens the second set, followed by a bouncy Woman Are Smarter [25]
- **High Time** (1 review): Garcia sings High Time with great heartfelt emotion, called a jewel of the show [25]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 other source): Noted as the last version of Lost Sailor; Saint is described as tight like a Swiss watch [4]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Morning Dew closes the second set, which the reviewer praises for its emotional vocals [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-03-24.nak300.mandel.79610.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 122 min [1]
- **gd1986-03-24.179300.senn.441.strizak.flac2448**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 125 min [2]
- **gd86-03-24.sbd.miller.22783.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 118 min; rated 2.71/5 by 7 [8]
- **gd86-03-24.naks.braverman.16746.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 113 min; rated 3.75/5 by 12 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this Nak audience source fuller and better balanced than the other two audience sources; Recording has bright highs and gritty low end; reviewer calls it the best source; Crisp Nak mics, but levels were boosted too far, causing substantial clipping that home CD players may mask [24][25][28][29]
- **gd86-03-24.schoeps.nawrocki.17890.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 18 songs; 117 min; rated 2.33/5 by 3 [16]. Said about its sound: Good audience tape with some hollow arena sound typical of the Spectrum, which reviewer says matched the live experience [27]

## Around the show

- Attendee was surprised at only one song after drums/space; a balloon popped during Ramble On Rose, drawing applause [31]
- Reviewer recalls attending with friends on a cold Monday night, after returning from a wedding [33]
- Uploader gives a birthday greeting to Anne Touliatos [2]
- Only one song follows space; crowd booed for more music after the encore [4]
- Of the other two sources, the Nawrocki one is judged better; reviewer also says a soundboard exists [24]
- Reviewer considers this about as good as 1986 shows get [26]
- Reviewer calls it the best show they saw in 1986, though a bit short [29]
- Attendee knew Box of Rain had been played in Hampton but thought it might be a one-off [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-03-24.nak300.mandel.79610.shnf**: taped by Brian Mandel; transferred by Brian Mandel; source: Nakamichi 300 Shotguns CP4's & Sony TCD5M [1]
- **gd1986-03-24.179300.senn.441.strizak.flac2448**: taped by Tom Strizak; transferred by Tom Strizak; source: Tom Strizak Master Cassettes (2) Senn. 441 mics at approx. 7’ height standard stereo configuration > Sony TC-D5M (2-Maxell Metal MX90 / Dolby-B). Location:… [2]. Also: Source has pauses between songs, with tape flips at end of Ramble On Rose and during Drums [2]
- **gd86-03-24.sbd.miller.22783.sbeok.shnf**: source: Source Info: SBD -> Cassette Master -> ? -> Cassette -> CD -> EAC -> SHN -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> SHNPatch Info: Schoeps CMC4/MK4 -> Cassette Master… [8]. Also: Matrix has audience patches for part of El Paso, all of Drums and all of Morning Dew [30]
- **gd86-03-24.naks.braverman.16746.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Master Cassette (Nakamichi 300 / Sony D5M) > Nakamichi BX-300 > CD > SHNThis is a new seed, with sector boundary errors fixed but otherwise no… [10]. Also: Reviewer's own old cassettes are soundboard for set one and set two through drums [24]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1986-03-24 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1986-03-24-backstage-pass/) [37]

claims.text: Reviewer finds this Nak audience source fuller and better balanced than the other two audience sources
Of the other two sources, the Nawrocki one is judged better; reviewer also says a soundboard exists
Reviewer's own old cassettes are soundboard for set one and set two through drums
Recording has bright highs and gritty low end; reviewer calls it the best source
Emotional Half-Step opens the second set, followed by a bouncy Woman Are Smarter
Garcia sings High Time with great heartfelt emotion, called a jewel of the show
Saint is described as super rockin' in a strong second set
Morning Dew closes the second set, which the reviewer praises for its emotional vocals
Reviewer considers this about as good as 1986 shows get
Good audience tape with some hollow arena sound typical of the Spectrum, which reviewer says matched the live experience
Crisp Nak mics, but levels were boosted too far, causing substantial clipping that home CD players may mask
Reviewer, who attended, singles out Box of Rain and the whole second set
Reviewer calls it the best show they saw in 1986, though a bit short
Reviewer describes the sound quality as reasonably good
Matrix has audience patches for part of El Paso, all of Drums and all of Morning Dew
Reviewer says this was the last Lost Sailor/Saint pairing with Garcia
Crowd erupted when Box of Rain began, and again when Phil's singing revealed what it was
Attendee was surprised at only one song after drums/space; a balloon popped during Ramble On Rose, drawing applause
Attendee knew Box of Rain had been played in Hampton but thought it might be a one-off
Attendee in press box seats recalls the roof coming off during Box of Rain
Reviewer notes fans knew Box of Rain was played in Hampton; Philadelphia showed practice made it better
Reviewer recalls attending with friends on a cold Monday night, after returning from a wedding
Source has pauses between songs, with tape flips at end of Ramble On Rose and during Drums
Uploader gives a birthday greeting to Anne Touliatos
A Promised Land tease comes before Greatest Story
Noted as the last version of Lost Sailor; Saint is described as tight like a Swiss watch
Only one song follows space; crowd booed for more music after the encore
